```{r}
if(require(rvest) == FALSE) install.packages("rvest")
if(require(dplyr) == FALSE) install.packages("dplyr")

mu_page <- rvest::read_html("https://miamioh.edu/policy-library/students/undergraduate/academic-regulations/index.html")

all_links <- mu_page |>
  rvest::html_elements("a")

link_preview <- dplyr::tibble(
  text = all_links |> rvest::html_text2(),
  href = all_links |> rvest::html_attr("href")
)

# Print ALL 220 rows so we can see the real pattern of the policy links
print(link_preview, n = 220)



```


```{r}
# Keep people older than 21
df |> dplyr::filter(age > 21)

# Keep only name and income
df |> dplyr::select(name, income)

# Create a new column
df |> dplyr::mutate(income_thousands = income / 1000)

# Sort from lowest to highest income
df |> dplyr::arrange(income)

# Calculate average income
df |> dplyr::summarise(avg_income = mean(income, na.rm = TRUE))

df[3, ]       # Third row, every column
df[, 2]       # Every row, second column
df[3, 2]      # Third row, second column
df$name       # The name column


lst[2]        # A list containing element 2
lst[[2]]      # The actual second element
lst$name      # The element named "name"
```

The 3 coding patterns I would learn first
These are especially valuable because the practice exam has three longer coding questions on scraping and APIs. Pasted text.txt

1. Scrape links from a webpage

```{r}
url <- "https://example.com"

mu_policies <- url |>
  rvest::read_html() |>
  rvest::html_elements("a") |>
  rvest::html_attr("href")
```

```{r}
# Keep rows where age is at least 21
df |> dplyr::filter(age >= 21)

# Keep only the name and GPA columns
df |> dplyr::select(name, GPA)

# Filter rows AND keep only certain columns
df |>
  dplyr::filter(age >= 21) |>  # Keep qualifying rows
  dplyr::select(name, GPA)     # Keep only these columns

# Create a new column
df |>
  dplyr::mutate(income_thousands = income / 1000)

# Sort from lowest to highest income
df |> dplyr::arrange(income)

# Sort from highest to lowest income
df |> dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(income))

# Calculate an average, ignoring missing values
df |>
  dplyr::summarise(avg_GPA = mean(GPA, na.rm = TRUE))

# Count rows in each category
df |> dplyr::count(major)

# Keep rows matching either condition
df |> dplyr::filter(age < 18 | age > 65)

# Keep rows matching BOTH conditions
df |> dplyr::filter(age >= 18 & GPA >= 3.0)

```


```{r}
# Example API URL (replace with the endpoint required by the question)
url <- "https://api.example.com/data"

# Send the request and parse the JSON response into an R object
response <- jsonlite::fromJSON(url)

# Inspect the returned object
str(response)

# Look at its names
names(response)

# Access a field inside a list
response$properties

# Access a nested field inside a list
response$properties$gridX

# Access a field inside a data frame
response$year

# Convert a simple response to a data frame
df <- as.data.frame(response)
```
